evidence.name: sub_53CBC0

function_ir.summary: Loads and validates a .MAS cube-map file: uppercases the given filename, opens it directly or by retrying across the registered path-prefix array (dword_8B8E30 entries at byte_8B5A3C, stride 132) with an "rb" mode string, reads the 12-byte header magic, and dispatches on it. A Cubemas410 magic allocates a 308-byte physics object, initializes it, parses the file, and links the object into a singly linked list rooted at dword_8B8F14 (next link at offset 304); other magics report an incorrect-file error. On any open failure it formats an "Error opening MAS file" message and reports -2. Widely called by cockpit/pit/UI setup paths.

local_names.a1: optional output pointer receiving the allocated object
local_names.v5: open file handle result from sub_587DB0
local_names.v11: result of sub_55FC40 (file parse), dispatch key

operations.description: If a2 is null or its first character is NUL, return 0 immediately.
Copy the input filename a2 into the local SrcStr buffer, including the terminating NUL.
Uppercase-normalize SrcStr via sub_589901 before opening.
Attempt to open the file: v5 = sub_587DB0(SrcStr, aRb), with aRb as the read-mode string.

If the direct open failed, retry across registered path prefixes: for each of dword_8B8E30 entries starting at byte_8B5A3C with stride 132, format "%s\\%s" (prefix + SrcStr) into v17 via StringFormatWithBufferOverflowCheck and retry sub_587DB0; stop on first success or when the counter reaches dword_8B8E30.
If no prefix produced an open handle, format "Error opening MAS file %s" into v17 and call sub_53C590(-2, v17); return -2.
Read 12 bytes of header into v15 with ThreadSafeReadWrapper_803f(v15, 1, 12, v5), then close the file with FileCloseWithLock(v5).
If the 12-byte header matches the Cubemas410 magic (strcmp(v15, aCubemas410) == 0), take the cube-map creation path.
Allocate a 308-byte object: v9 = OperatorNewNhMallocWrapper(308); if non-null, initialize it via sub_55FBE0(v9) into v10, else v10 = 0.
Parse the file by name: v11 = sub_55FC40(SrcStr); the returned code drives the dispatch below.
On parse result -2 or -1: if the object v10 exists, run EmptyStub_7470(v10) then FreeWrapper_7bcf(v10); return -2 (resp. -1).

On parse result 0 (success): append v10 to the object list. If dword_8B8F14 is non-null, walk the singly linked list (next pointers at offset 304) to the tail and store v10 as the tail's next, plus set v10's back-pointer at dword index 75 (offset 300); otherwise make v10 the new list head dword_8B8F14.
Increment the global object count dword_8B6AC0 and set the local result to 0.
If a1 is non-null, write the created object pointer to *a1; return the local result.
If the header matched neither the Cubemas400 nor the Cubemas401 magic, return 0 without further action.
For the remaining magics, report an incorrect-file error: sub_53C590(-2, aIncorrectMasFi) and return -1.
